answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it earns rewards, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation should then grow slowly from real, verifiable work — like a nebula condensing from scattered dust into a star — rather than from sheer numbers. When an agent is caught cheating, its stake is slashed and its record is marked in umber, a permanent stain peers can see. At its nadir, a bad actor loses both money and standing, which makes honest participation the cheaper path.
